_note: The shot plan for RefinaNose, "It Wasn't the Nose". Hand-authored; gen/shots.py validates it, emits shots.ts, and verifies a render against it. `lines` is how many script phrases the beat covers and is the single declaration of beat structure — beats.ts derives its bounds from here, so docs/scripts/nose.txt, words-vo.ts and this file cannot disagree without failing at module load.
_argument: The eye does not size a feature, it compares one to the ones around it. So a nose that reads as too big can be a lower third that reads as too small. Measured on this pair: nose 9.7, lips 17.3, eyes 18.7, jaw 44.0, concentration 2.36, drift 4.7 — the nose is the QUIETEST of the four regions and under a quarter of the jaw, which is what earns the line 'almost none of it is on her nose'. gen/emit-nose.py refuses to write measured.ts if that stops being true.
_length: flip-v6 was rejected at 88.1s as 'long and thin' against a corpus median of 55.5s. RefinaRatio makes this same argument at 92.3s because it spends six of nine beats on three numbered relationships. This is the single-argument cut: one relationship, developed, and the read comes back at 52.3s.
_evidence: Every figure on screen comes from gen/emit-nose.py via measured.ts and describes two IMAGE FILES, never a face (rule E). The proof beat's map is gen/diffmap.py, masked to the same facial-skin pixels region_score measures over — rule Z, which RefinaFlip learned by shipping a map that lit the hairline while its chips reported skin.
_no_spans: THIS REEL DRAWS NO SPANS, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A STYLE CHOICE. RefinaLips brackets a philtrum because its claim is that a vertical distance shortens. Measured on this pair the lower third does NOT change height — face height 1070 -> 1059 px, nose-base-to-chin 375 -> 375 px — while lower-face WIDTH goes 572 -> 628. A bracket across the lower third would therefore have drawn a difference that is not there and passed every check in the repo (invariant HH). The width figure is real but its own instrument reports the untouched EYE LINE moving 739 -> 788 px, so its edges are contaminated and it cannot carry a printed claim either. The face itself is annotated with `Ring` only, which says WHERE and never HOW MUCH.
_motion: Five of eight beats are declared moving, 59% of runtime. Every one of them is a travelling HARD EDGE, never a dissolve: invariant BB records that a blend between two near-identical pictures crosses no threshold at all and a whole-frame transform scores as a CUT. Invariant KK then says a wipe moves only where the two pictures DIFFER — which is why this pair is easier than lips: the mouth is a narrow central band but the lower third spans the full width of the face, so a vertical seam registers change across most of its travel. `mechanism`, `test` and `cta` are declared static because a still photograph with overlays arriving on top IS static however many arrive, and declaring otherwise then adding a creep to satisfy the check is rule P exactly.
_device: The travelling seam RECURS — `hook` and `resolve` are the same composition doing the same thing at the two ends of the argument, and `claim` runs it on the other axis. Gemini counted 17 devices with none used twice in ours-changed-v2 against a corpus median of 11 with at least one repeated.
_subject: ONE subject, deliberately. The two-subject rule exists because RefinaChanged silently changed who its subject was three times; it does not require a second face. The script says 'the same woman' and 'same nose, both photographs', and keeping that literally true for the whole runtime is worth more here than an announced second casting.
_framing: EVERY PORTRAIT BEAT IS FRAMED DIFFERENTLY, AND THAT IS A FINDING FROM refs/analyse.py. The first cut ran hook, claim, proof and resolve all at fit 0.75, and the Gemini pass described beats 1-5 as ONE 37-second scene: 'full-bleed portrait with split-screen slider'. The recurring seam is deliberate (device recurrence, per the ours-changed-v2 finding), but recurrence plus identical framing stops reading as a signature and starts reading as one long take — which is what 'long and thin' meant when flip-v6 was rejected. The sizes now step 0.72 -> 0.84 -> 0.66 -> 0.55 -> 0.78, and each move is motivated: `claim` pushes in because it is the beat that names the chin, `proof` pulls back to make room for the readout, `mechanism` sits at medium because its line is about the whole face. This is NOT a creep added to move a number (rule P) - it is a cut decision, applied per beat, that the measurement asked for.
_shot_sizes: `proof` is declared MEDIUM rather than close, and the render is why: pulled back far enough to carry the bar readout it measures 0.302, just under the 0.310 close floor. The bands are terciles of 1268 corpus frames, not preferences, so the honest move is to declare what the beat actually is rather than nudge `fit` up two points to clear a boundary — which would have moved the number without changing the shot (rule P). It sits next to `mechanism`, also medium, but the two share no look at all: a dark false-colour map under a four-column readout, then a photograph with two rings on it.
_mechanism:
`mechanism` carries a comparison band — a soft sweep travelling between the two measured ring edges for the rest of the beat, which is the line 'your eye doesn't measure features, it compares them' drawn rather than only said. It is nonetheless declared STATIC, because --verify measured it at 1%% of frames moving.

That is invariant L, confirmed rather than assumed: three stills 26 frames apart put the band at three visibly different heights, with 1.65-1.75 mean pixel change between them. It moves and a viewer sees it. What it does not do is clear the tile threshold at 270x480, which needs a mean change above 3.0 inside a tile, and a 26%%-opacity gradient over a picture at fit 0.55 does not reach that.

The band STAYS and the declaration changes. Raising its opacity until the check passed would be tuning the reel to the instrument — the exact move rule P records against mirror2, where a slow zoom was added to every held beat to bring a frozen number down and neither worked nor would have been a fix. A beat is `moving` only if its picture measurably changes on its own; this one's does not, and saying so is the point of declaring it.
_nuance: `nuance` runs at fit 0.44, not 0.36. At 0.36 the two cards were 389px wide inside a 1080px frame and the beat was a pair of postage stamps adrift in sage — spec rule 5's 'small element floating in a large empty field', and rule Q's point that occupancy is the number to fix first because frozen, cuts and arrivals all follow it. gen/check-frames.py found it as 139 consecutive frames whose top edge was one flat colour. At 0.44 the two cards reach both margins at full separation and the face still measures inside the WIDE band, which is what the beat needs to carry the reel's shot travel.
_background: THE PICTURE'S BACKGROUND IS THE STAGE. gen/sage.py repaints each master's studio backdrop (177,197,208) to the exact stage sage (163,181,186) by solving the composite rather than keying to alpha, so hair edges un-mix instead of fringing. Measured over the face mask the repaint moves 0.4% of skin pixels by a mean of 0.012 levels -- the subject is untouched, which is why the evidence is still computed from the unpadded pair.
_frame: THE PICTURE COVERS THE FRAME AND THERE IS NO `fit`. Once the backdrop matches the stage the top and side edges vanish and the BOTTOM does not: the black turtleneck runs to it and stops in mid-air, with promote.py's 167px pad below that (invariant T). It cannot be framed out -- centred, the shoulders only clear the frame bottom at fit >= 1.21, which puts the face at 0.57 against a close band topping out at 0.453. So gen/extend-pad.py clamps the last flat content row down, and gen/extend-frame.py pads the canvas to 2764x4900 until the face is 0.208 of a frame the picture now covers. Framing is then `zoom` + a `focus` solved from the record, which anchors.ts ALREADY models -- so every ring, seam and band follows the camera for free instead of needing a second transform kept in step by hand (invariant S).
_push: TWO BEATS PUSH IN ON THE FEATURE THEY NAME, and this is not the zoom rule P forbids. That rule came from mirror2, where a slow zoom was added to every held beat -- beats with nothing in them -- purely to move a frozen-frame number, and it neither worked nor would have been a fix. These start on the SCRIPT LINE that names a feature and travel to that feature's measured box: `claim` to the chin as it says 'her chin is what moved', `resolve` to the nose as it says 'the nose has something to sit against'. They are done for the edit. If the motion figures do not move, or move the wrong way, the push stays and the numbers are reported as they are.
_wide: THE WIDE SHOT IS NOT A SHRUNKEN PORTRAIT, AND INVARIANT Y SAYS WHY: the references get their range by cutting to compositions that are NOT portraits -- index cards, real-world photographs, insets -- not by resizing the same face. The first attempt here did resize it, and the picture ran out of subject: a head-and-shoulders crop has no chest, so a canvas tall enough for a 0.21 face filled its bottom third with 1340px of clamped turtleneck. The masters are now padded only as far as MEDIUM (face 0.257 at zoom 1) and `nuance`'s two panels carry the wide end, because a panel crops the picture rather than shrinking it.
_zoom_calibration: THE ZOOMS ARE SET FROM THE RENDER, NOT FROM THE ARITHMETIC. The face box in the asset record is 0.257 of frame at zoom 1, but gen/shots.py measures with a Haar cascade that reads about 90% of that box, so the first pass at these numbers put four beats a hair under their bands (hook 0.304 against a 0.31 close floor). The bands are terciles of 1268 corpus frames and the detector is the thing that will judge the next render too, so the zooms are calibrated against what it actually reports rather than against the geometry it approximates.
